metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal secured another huge win as she continued her impressive comeback from long-term injury at the Wuhan Open.
metadata.content: Wuhan Open: Britain's Sonay Kartal earns huge win over Belinda Bencic to set up meeting with Jasmine Paolini in China | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Wuhan Open: Britain's Sonay Kartal earns huge win over Belinda Bencic to set up meeting with Jasmine Paolini in China Sonay Kartal beats world No 12 and former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic 6-0 7-5; Iga Swiatek also advances after defeating fellow Pole Magdalena Frech; watch WTA Wuhan Open and ATP Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports, with events running until Sunday Wednesday 14 October 2026 11:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sonay Kartal continued her impressive comeback from long-term injury with victory over Belinda Bencic at the Wuhan Open Britain's Sonay Kartal secured another huge win as she continued her impressive comeback from long-term injury at the Wuhan Open. The 24-year-old made a flying start against world No 12 and former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic in the second round in China, going on to claim a 6-0 7-5 victory. Kartal missed six months of the season with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in Shenzhen before reaching the third round in Beijing last week. messages.text: England Women's World Cup half-back dilemma

metadata.summary: If there is one position that highlights the growth of the women's game in England, it is the competition for the half-back spot at the Rugby League World Cup.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England Women's half-back dilemma as Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche head into competition in form | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Rugby League World Cup: England Women's half-back dilemma as Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche head into competition in form England Women have three outstanding half-back options for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup, with Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche all vying for a place in the side; their campaign gets under way against Wales on October 17 with Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche starting Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Wednesday 14 October 2026 06:51, UK Image: Georgia Roche, Jenna Foubister and Izzy Rowe - credit SWpix If there is one position that highlights the growth of the women's game in England, it is the competition for the half-back spot at the Rugby League World Cup. Two Wigan stars provide one option, with Woman of Steel Jenna Foubister joined by her best friend and Warriors half-back partner Izzy Rowe. Then there's NRLW star and former Woman of Steel Georgia Roche, who has been tearing it up on the other side of the world. It is a selection headache that England Women head coach Stuart Barrow welcomes as he prepares his side for three pool games, with a place in the semi-finals at stake. messages.text: British and Irish Lions Women to face France in first match

metadata.summary: The British and Irish Lions Women's team will face France at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Friday August 27, marking the first-ever match played by a Lions Women's team.
metadata.content: British and Irish Lions Women: Cardiff's Principality Stadium to host team's first-ever match against France | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content British and Irish Lions Women: Cardiff's Principality Stadium to host team's first-ever match against France The British and Irish Lions Women's team will play their first ever match against France on August 27 in 2027; The match will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff before they head on their first ever Tour to New Zealand Wednesday 14 October 2026 11:03, UK Image: British and Irish Lions Women will play France at the Principality Stadium before their tour of New Zealand The British and Irish Lions Women's team will face France at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Friday August 27, marking the first-ever match played by a Lions Women's team. The Howden Lions Women's Cup will provide supporters with their first opportunity to see Jo Yapp's side in action on home soil ahead of the inaugural Tour to New Zealand in 2027. The Tour begins Saturday September 4 when the Lions Women face a Black Ferns XV at Semenoff Stadium in Whangārei, before the historic first Test against the Black Ferns at Go Media Stadium in Auckland on Saturday September 11.
